title: EventEnvelope.v1
description: Normative envelope for every domain event published on the platform (A§24). Exactly these ten fields — nothing else is permitted on the wire. The envelope is transport-agnostic: it is the Kafka message value on `collections.<context>` and `ingestion.*` topics (A§25), and the same JSON is stored in the transactional outbox and replayed from the DLQ. Ordering is guaranteed only per aggregate (A§26): the partition key is defined per event type by the topic/key map (contracts/asyncapi/collections.v1.yaml) and is normally `aggregateId`. `payload` is intentionally unconstrained here and is validated separately against `schemas/events/<context>/<eventType>.v<eventVersion>.json`. Released contract files are immutable: a breaking change ships as EventEnvelope.v2.json (D§29).

eventId.description: Identity of this event instance, assigned once by the producer and never reused. Written to the outbox `event_id` UNIQUE column and used by consumers for inbox dedupe on (consumer, eventId), which is what makes at-least-once delivery safe (D§3.5). Redeliveries of the same fact carry the same eventId; a genuinely new fact always gets a new one.

eventType.description: Business event name in PascalCase with no version suffix — the version lives in `eventVersion`. Must match the payload schema file name: `schemas/events/<context>/<eventType>.v<eventVersion>.json` (e.g. eventType `CaseCreated` + eventVersion 1 → schemas/events/case/CaseCreated.v1.json).

eventVersion.description: Major version of the payload contract for this eventType, starting at 1. The meaning of an existing (eventType, eventVersion) pair never changes: a breaking payload change ships as a new version and both run side by side until every consumer has migrated (D§29). Consumers must ignore unknown versions rather than fail.

occurredAt.description: When the business fact happened (not when it was published or consumed). RFC3339 date-time, always UTC with a `Z` offset and no local offsets.

producer.description: Service or component that emitted the event, in kebab-case, matching its deployable name (A§7.2 gives the single owning producer per event type — no event has two producers).

aggregateType.description: PascalCase type of the aggregate this event is about, as named in the canonical domain model (A§8).

aggregateId.description: Identifier of the aggregate instance (e.g. the caseId when aggregateType is `Case`). Non-empty; normally a ULID for platform-owned aggregates, but source-system identifiers are permitted for aggregates keyed by external references, so no pattern is imposed.

correlationId.description: Ties every hop of one business interaction together across HTTP, Kafka, Airflow and Snowflake QUERY_TAG (A§97). Propagated unchanged from the inbound X-Correlation-Id header or the consumed event; generated at the edge when absent. Also returned in API error bodies (A§20).

causationId.description: OPTIONAL — the direct cause of this event: the eventId of the event being handled, or the identity of the command that produced it (typically the Idempotency-Key of the originating POST, A§21). Omit the property entirely for the first event in a chain, which by definition has no in-platform cause (e.g. an event raised by an operator action or an inbound source record). Never send null — omit the field. Together with correlationId this forms the causation graph used by decision explainability and incident forensics.

payload.description: Event-type-specific body. Deliberately unconstrained by this schema and validated separately against `schemas/events/<context>/<eventType>.v<eventVersion>.json`, which is `additionalProperties: false` with explicit `required`. Must always be an object (never a scalar or array) so that payloads can be extended additively within a version.

ulid.title: ULID
ulid.description: ULID in canonical Crockford base32 form: 26 uppercase characters, excluding I, L, O and U. Lexicographically sortable by generation time.
